answer: Sequential work-thread binding. Each agent identity gets a single economic thread: to transact it must first complete a publicly verifiable work unit whose output is consumed by the next task in line, chaining identities. A clone cannot skip ahead; it must reproduce the entire prior chain or wait. This whispers a hard floor on marginal cost. Every new identity must also purchase a fresh ledge of scarce compute credits at auction, and the price rises with chain depth.
